title: Inspect and extend: Browser records and protection state
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/Models.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve tab, protection-level, and tracker data types.
problem: A browser model is a set of labels and settings the interface can render. Read the record types and identify which data belongs to a tab and which belongs to a protection mode. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/Models.swift` and the related project files: Sources/Models.swift; Sources/Core.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to tab, protection-level, and tracker data types.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The sample model is not the complete Firefox account/profile model.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A browser model is a set of labels and settings the interface can render. Read the record types and identify which data belongs to a tab and which belongs to a protection mode.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/Models.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
